name: Sa Pa homestay trek: Ta Van to Ban Ho
region: Mường Hoa valley, Sa Pa, Lào Cai
why: Down the Mường Hoa valley from the Giáy village of Ta Van, through the Red Dao village of Giang Ta Chai and the hamlet of Su Pan, to a Tày stilt-house village, with a night there.
book: No permit. Go with a local guide or a tour from Sa Pa: the Lao Cai tourist information centre runs this walk as day 2 of a 3-day homestay trek. Most walkers sleep in Ta Van the night before (after the Lao Chai walk) and in a Ban Ho homestay at the end; transfer back to Sa Pa by car.
water: Drinks and lunch in Giang Ta Chai and Su Pan; dinner at the homestay in Ban Ho. Carry 1.5 litres.
dangers: Muddy, slippery clay paths and paddy dykes after rain: shoes with good grip.
Hanging bridges over the streams: one at a time.
Sections on the valley road with motorbikes and trucks.
Cold, wet fog from November to February; floods in heavy summer rain.
turnaround: If the river is in flood or rain is heavy, stop in Su Pan and ride the valley road to Ban Ho.

points.name: Ta Van
points.note: The Giáy village on the valley floor at about 1,000 m, full of homestays. The path leaves east along the river through the paddies.

points.name: Giang Ta Chai
points.note: Red Dao village, known for red embroidery and silver coins on the clothes. Near it: a waterfall, a cane hanging bridge and a protected bamboo forest.

points.name: Su Pan
points.note: A hamlet with a school and a few homestays, the usual lunch stop. From here the trail goes on down the valley, crossing the Mường Hoa river.

points.name: Ban Ho stream
points.note: Ban Ho, a Tày and Red Dao village of stilt houses where the streams meet. Night in a homestay; a hot spring near the village.
